security_audit.summary: Most external command alerts are Markdown or inline-code false positives, and the high-entropy alert is a false positive for multilingual Markdown. Four command-related alerts are confirmed for `git pull` and Gradle execution because they can mutate the workspace or run project code; no malicious intent, exfiltration, or prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Repository update command can mutate the working tree.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running `git pull origin main`, and remind users to protect local changes first.

remediation.issue: Gradle validation and server commands execute project code.
remediation.suggestion: Gate `./gradlew check` and `./gradlew bootRun` behind user approval, with a warning that project scripts may execute local code.

remediation.issue: Command examples are mixed with documentation examples.
remediation.suggestion: Separate shell commands from file path references and add brief safety notes for commands that modify state or start services.

content.user_title: Build Spring Boot Backends with MyBatis
content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent Spring Boot APIs, database changes, tests, and documentation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through that workflow.
actual_capabilities: Plans REST controller, service, mapper, entity, and DTO work for Spring Boot.
Guides Flyway migration creation and database design updates.
Requires OpenAPI, error code, and database documentation updates.
Prompts JUnit, Mockito, MyBatis, lint, and coverage checks.
Directs reuse of utility classes, exception handlers, and logging aspects.
limitations: Targets a specific Spring Boot and MyBatis project structure.
Requires human approval before running Git or Gradle commands.
Does not replace project-specific security review or database approval.
Assumes Japanese project documentation and workflow conventions.

use_cases.title: Implement Feature APIs
use_cases.description: Add controller, service, mapper, DTO, migration, and tests for a backend feature.

use_cases.title: Maintain Database Changes
use_cases.description: Coordinate Flyway migrations, database design updates, and related API documentation.

use_cases.title: Validate Delivery Quality
use_cases.description: Check lint, tests, coverage, server startup, and completion evidence before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a simple read-only REST API for [feature]. Explain the files you will inspect before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to implement [feature] with a controller, service, DTOs, mapper, and tests. Ask before running Git or Gradle commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Database Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a Flyway migration for [database change], update database-design.md, and keep OpenAPI and error codes aligned.

prompt_templates.title: Deliver an End-to-End Backend Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to deliver [complex feature] end to end. Include branch checks, utility reuse, approved validation, and the completion report.

output_examples.input: Add a user profile endpoint with persistence and validation.
output: Implementation plan covering controller, service, mapper, DTO, migration, and tests.
Documentation checklist for OpenAPI, database design, and error codes.
Validation summary with lint, test, coverage, and server startup status.

output_examples.input: Review a backend change before handoff.
output: Risk notes for unused code, duplicate logging, and unnecessary try-catch blocks.
Confirmation checklist for branch, issue number, coverage, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Create a Flyway migration for a new table.
output: Migration planning notes with table, column, and naming considerations.
Related mapper, entity, DTO, and documentation update list.
Test and rollback review points for the database change.

best_practices: Confirm the branch and issue number before editing backend files.
Reuse existing utilities, exception handlers, and logging aspects before adding new patterns.
Request approval before commands that update Git state or execute Gradle tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not invent authentication, cookie, logging, or exception helpers before checking existing utilities.
Do not add duplicate request or SQL logging already handled by AOP.
Do not skip documentation, error code updates, or coverage checks after backend changes.

faq.question: What kind of backend does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Spring Boot backends that use MyBatis, Flyway, JUnit, Mockito, and Gradle validation.

faq.question: Can it design new database tables?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides table and column planning, Flyway migration creation, and database design documentation updates.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It may suggest Git or Gradle commands, but users should approve commands before execution.

faq.question: Does it help with tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for unit tests, mapper tests when useful, lint checks, and coverage review.

faq.question: Is this only for new features?
faq.answer: No. It can also support fixes, refactors, documentation updates, and delivery validation.

faq.question: What should users prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare a clear task, issue number, target branch, API expectations, and any database requirements.
